page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate performance across standard compute and memory tasks. The instance achieves average results in Geekbench single-core (1315.0) and multi-core (5025.0) tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 10249.39. However, raw synthetic CPU performance shows limitations, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks falling into the poor and weak categories, respectively. Memory bandwidth is mixed; cached small-block reads perform at an average rate of 395.92 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block reads and writes are weaker, registering at 32.16 GB/sec and 16.75 GB/sec.

Given its compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6a.2xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for workloads that prioritize processing cores over large memory footprints. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of high-capacity RAM or GPU hardware. Suitable workloads include static web serving (benchmarked at 6.78 GB/sec), software compilation (Geekbench clang score of 7237.0), Redis operations (7.44 million operations/sec), and moderate database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 2.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, relying instead on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks position the instance in the average tier for Geekbench multi-core (5025.0) and PassMark CPU (10249.39) tests, though synthetic stress-ng CPU metrics are weak. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a resource-dense option for compute-focused tasks. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, Redis key-value stores, and moderate database operations that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage.
